title: Panel selection
contract: Selecting a shell section changes its detail display; Noise has no separate detail display. The Global MPE switch reveals Pressure, Slide and NotePB controls. This specifies presentation, not synthesis structure.

title: Shape and LFO control eligibility
contract: Pulse Width is editable for the rectangular oscillator shape; oscillator Width-LFO and Pitch-LFO modulation controls require their corresponding LFO enabled. The existing oscillator laws are not restated.

title: Quick Routing and preserved edits
contract: Quick Routing selects four layouts: upper-left gives each oscillator its own filter/amplifier; upper-right sends each oscillator to both filters; lower-left sends both to Filter 1/Amp 1 only; lower-right sends both through Filter 1 into Filter 2/Amp 2. The gesture preserves oscillator level, tuning and waveform edits. Exact signal coefficients remain with the Analog owner.

title: Filter Follow control context
contract: Filter 2 Follow changes its cutoff control to an offset from Filter 1, including the documented following of Filter 1 cutoff modulation. Exact tracking and modulation arithmetic remain U here.

title: Envelope modes beyond finite renders
contract: Envelope Legato reuses the current envelope position for overlapping notes; Free skips sustain. Loop offers Off, AD-R, ADR-R and ADS-R; Free in AD-R/ADR-R treats notes as held, while ADS-R repeats attack/release at key release. These documentary mode roles do not supply curves, timing or a target reset law.

title: LFO timing and shape controls
contract: Each LFO offers Hz/sync rate, Delay/Attack and Retrig/Offset. Width is editable for triangle/rectangle and disabled for sine/noise. Existing free-running waveform laws are not expanded by these UI and sync descriptions.

title: Vibrato activation and wheel amount
contract: Vibrato activation exposes its additional controls; Amt < MW is relative to the shell Vibrato Amount. Error describes per-voice random variation without a distribution or reproducibility rule.

title: Unison workflow
contract: Uni enables additional Unison Voices/Delay controls and Detune variation. These are stacked-voice controls, distinct from keyboard polyphony; no voice-budget formula or delayed-onset tolerance is added.

title: Glide workflow
contract: Gli exposes Glide Mode; Legato limits slides to overlapping notes. Const and Prop distinguish interval-independent versus interval-dependent glide time, without an interpolation or first-note law.

title: MPE destinations and bend controls
contract: Pressure and Slide each offer two destinations with individual amounts and input-activity LEDs. Note PB sets per-note bend range, separately from global PB Range. Destinations/domains/codecs not established by this text remain U.

title: Tabs and presentation
contract: Resonator, LFO and MIDI/MPE tabs expose their corresponding controls, alongside global voice/retrigger/structure/output controls. The existing resonator-order and finite voice laws remain with the Collision owner.

title: Resonator-dependent eligibility
contract: Object selection updates the X-Y visualization. Pipe/Tube omit Quality and replace Material with Radius; their Brightness/Inharm/Hit/listening controls are not used. Ratio is for Membrane/Plate and Opening for Pipe. These are visible eligibility/role statements, not new modal or waveguide laws.

title: Resonator copy buttons
contract: Each resonator has a directional copy button that copies its settings to the other resonator. This establishes exposed value copying, not an atomic transaction, tail copy or private-state cloning.

title: LFO destinations and retrigger controls
contract: The two LFOs can target parameters and each other; each has two destination amounts relative to overall Amount. Rate supports Hz/sync; Offset sets the retrigger start phase. No lookup, scaling formula, random law or clock boundary is inferred.

title: MIDI and MPE mapping destinations
contract: Pitch bend/per-note bend, wheel, pressure and slide can each map to two destinations with independent amounts; Key/Vel controls supply additional parameter modulation. No message codec, destination list or response law is invented.

title: Repeated-note Retrig workflow
contract: Global Retrig is documented to retrigger an already-playing note rather than add a voice. Duplicate-note pairing, release velocity and target allocation remain U and do not expand the existing finite voice contract.

title: Model-dependent control presentation
contract: Model selection changes control eligibility: Pipe/Tube use Radius instead of Material and omit Quality/Bright/Inharm/Hit/listening/Bleed roles; Opening is Pipe-only and Ratio Membrane/Plate-only. Existing numerical model/position laws remain authoritative elsewhere.

title: Sidechain access and MIDI source
contract: The title-bar toggle opens MIDI sidechain controls and indicates active sidechain use. MIDI From selects a source track and tap point; Frequency and Off Decay enable distinct modulation roles.

title: Frequency mode and note priority
contract: Frequency-enabled sidechain follows MIDI note tuning with Last/Low priority for held notes and coarse/fine offsets plus PB Range. With Frequency off, Tune controls Hertz and a note/cents readout is shown. This adds documentary controls/roles, not a note-frequency or priority scheduling formula.

title: Off Decay admission
contract: Off Decay makes MIDI Note Off reduce resonance according to its amount; the endpoints are described as ignoring Note Off versus muting it. No numeric decay, immediate deadline, sustain-pedal or held-note aggregation policy is established for the target.

title: Synchronized LFO and stereo eligibility
contract: Sync exposes Offset; Spin is available only in Hz mode, where Phase/Spin can be selected. For noise waveforms Phase/Spin are described as ineffective; this is not random-sample identity or a new free-running waveform formula.

title: Dry/Wet and running resonance
contract: The manual describes Dry/Wet as changing admission of new input without cutting resonances already sounding. This dynamic documentary statement does not replace the existing constant-parameter mix law or establish a tail-preservation tolerance.

title: Limiter indication
contract: A LED next to Gain is documented as indicating automatic limiting at excessive level. No threshold, curve, ceiling, clipping rule or real-time performance oracle follows.

title: Tabs, section toggles and shared Volume
contract: String and Filter/Global tabs expose their named sections; all sections except String and Keyboard have independent enables. The overall Volume is accessible from both tabs. No CPU saving or independent duplicate Volume parameter is required.

title: Exciter-dependent controls
contract: The first exciter controls depend on selected type: Bow Force/Friction, Hammer variants Mass/Stiffness and Plectrum Protrusion/Stiffness. Damping is unavailable for Bow. Existing exciter models/ranges remain with their owners.

title: Damper Gated and Velocity eligibility
contract: Damper Velocity is effective/enabled in the documented Gated context; Gated off leaves the damper applied and Velocity has no stated effect. The finite damper/decay law is not redefined.

title: Filter modulation subsection gates
contract: Filter, Filter Envelope and Filter LFO have independent switches. The LFO/Env modulation sliders have no effect unless their corresponding subsections are enabled. No filter coefficient or modulation scaling law is added.

title: Filter LFO sync and onset controls
contract: The filter LFO offers Hz/sync rate and Delay/Attack onset controls. Random choices are described but provide no seed, distribution or new waveform comparator.

title: Vibrato wheel and Error controls
contract: Vibrato has an enable, Delay/Attack and Rate/Amount controls; wheel depth is relative to Amount and Error adds unspecified variation. Existing finite render-defined modulation does not cover these controller interactions.

title: MPE destinations, indicators and bend ranges
contract: Pressure and Slide each have two destination/amount slots; pressure/slide/note-bend activity LEDs indicate input. Global Pitch Bend and Note PB ranges are distinct. MPE destination domains, codec and audio remain unknown.

title: Portamento and Legato workflow
contract: Portamento enable/Time and Legato select note-slide context; Prop makes time interval-dependent while off is constant-time. This documentary role does not provide first-note behavior, a curve or a timing tolerance.

title: Unison workflow
contract: Unison enables stacked-voice Voices, Detune and Delay controls, distinct from Keyboard polyphony. No stacked-voice allocation budget or onset/detune formula is specified here.

title: Gain, Volume and tonal interactions
contract: Gain is the principal distortion control while Volume addresses output; EQ controls interact and Presence is model-dependent. These are documented control roles, not independent gain stages, transfer curves, coefficients or a private circuit requirement.

title: Output processing selector
contract: Output selects mono or Dual processing. The CPU multiplier in the prose is context only; channel mapping and performance criteria are unknown. Labels/domains stay with the parameter owner.

title: Separate and companion placement
contract: Amp and Cabinet may be used independently; the manual recommends Cabinet after Amp for the companion setup. This is an optional workflow, not automatic insertion or a required guitar-only input.
